correctness.rationale: The general theorem is proved by taking selected neighbours of each unselected vertex along its diameter-at-most-three geodesic witness, then covering every edge by a one-, two-, or three-edge selected-endpoint geodesic. The three-edge case uses bipartiteness and no four-cycles critically. The Fano geometry is explicitly modelled on 14 vertices and every one of 16384 subsets is enumerated in two independent checkers. One constructs paths, the other tests distance equations. Both reproduce the all-set coefficients and minimal cardinality counts; explicit projective masks match precisely all 65 minimal sets. Boundary K3,3 is an actual failure example.

Earlier general plane work already proves the minimum 4 and its 21 flag bases, which are explicitly attributed and excluded as new priority. No accessible primary theorem or indexed result implied the stronger equivalence; unavailable full text and unindexed history are retained as genuine risks.

value.rationale: The theorem collapses two distinct natural shortest-path covering predicates set by set on an infinite class containing incidence graphs of every finite projective plane, stronger than matching minimum cardinalities. Four-cycle-freeness is essential by an explicit K3,3 boundary example. The 65-set Heawood classification and polynomial give naturally motivated nonpure extremal information (minimum and upper minimal cardinalities 4 and 7), not an arbitrary small slice or routine substitution.
